actions.reason: The K4_C0001-K4_C0004 boundary is the weakest and most internally conflicting of the decision-relevant neighbors. Structural diagnostics for this pair show the highest normalized-cut cost (0.550, i.e. greatest cross-boundary connectivity) and a union eigengap profile dominated by the single-cluster resolution (candidate_k=1, leading gap 0.492), which is merge-compatible and must not be read as preserving two units (ER:d2497140466c:cross_modal_consistency:structural_diagnostics:pair:aad94ea7bd). Native patient geometry for this boundary disagrees materially: CT shows negative separation (silhouette -0.027, negative fraction 0.596) while RNA/WSI/WXS show only weak positive separation (ER:d2497140466c:cross_modal_consistency:affinity_geometry_concordance:pair:aad94ea7bd). Membership representation is likewise weak/conflicting for both sets: K4_C0001 is directionally mixed with CT negative (silhouette -0.094, negative fraction 1.0) and only small positive RNA/WSI/WXS values, with K4_C0004 as the nearest competing set (ER:d2497140466c:cross_modal_consistency:affinity_geometry_concordance:set:e5313ac502); K4_C0004 is conflicting with WXS strongly positive but RNA and WSI negative and CT only weakly positive (ER:d2497140466c:cross_modal_consistency:affinity_geometry_concordance:set:6e0bda1ea1). The current boundary is therefore weak/conflicting and the union is more consistent with a single unit, supporting a provisional merge of K4_C0001 and K4_C0004.

actions.reason: The K4_C0002|K4_C0003 boundary is the strongest structural pair candidate (mean between-affinity 0.193) and its exact-pair evidence is merge-compatible: normalized-cut cost is substantial (0.532) indicating appreciable cross-boundary connectivity, and the union eigengap shows candidate_k=2 (leading gap 0.487), i.e. the union resolves as a single two-cluster structure rather than two independently retained units. Membership representation is weak-to-conflicting for both sets: K4_C0002 shows one weakly positive view (CT 0.046) and three non-separating views (RNA -0.055, WSI -0.047, WXS -0.054), and K4_C0003 shows two weak-to-modest positive views (RNA 0.133, CT 0.056) and two non-separating views (WSI -0.047, WXS -0.007), with disagreement on the nearest neighbor in both. The pair boundary representation is likewise weak and mixed (CT modest 0.143, RNA/WSI/WXS near zero with substantial negative fractions). The transcriptomic phenotypes are coherent but complementary rather than contradictory (K4_C0002: OXPHOS/fatty-acid/mTORC1/adipogenesis up; K4_C0003: immune/inflammatory programs up), which is consistent with a single unit containing two biological facets and does not prohibit merge. No exact-pair evidence supports preserving this boundary as two independent discovery units, so the provisional revision is a merge of K4_C0002 and K4_C0003.

actions.reason: Membership representation is weak and largely negative: CT (-0.028, negative fraction 0.745), WSI (-0.072, 0.863), and WXS (-0.057, 0.412) all place these patients closer to the competing set than to their own, with only weak positive RNA (0.053). The pair boundary is only weakly represented and partially conflicting (WXS 0.125, RNA 0.061, CT/WSI near zero with high negative fractions), so independence from the neighboring set is not established. Candidate-specific technical alternatives remain plausible: tissue source site, CT phase, and CT manufacturer are all significantly associated (q 0.036) with no adjustment or persistence analysis. The transcriptomic phenotype is coherent but is the reciprocal mirror of the other set in a two-set partition, so it is not independent biological confirmation and cannot rescue broadly unsupported membership. The internal-subdivision screen is ambiguous (k=2 gap 0.4867 vs k=1 gap 0.4224) and does not support a feasible meaningful split. With membership unsupported, boundary weak/conflicting, technical explanations unresolved, and no supported structural revision, this candidate lacks defensible discovery value.

This set has a substantive, interpretable biological identity: coordinated oxidative-phosphorylation down-regulation with down-regulation of interferon alpha/gamma, allograft rejection, complement, IL6/JAK/STAT3, ROS, apoptosis, coagulation, and DNA repair, plus up-regulation of TGF-beta, WNT/beta-catenin, Hedgehog, angiogenesis, and Notch (FDR q <= 0.05). Membership representation is coherent and weakly-to-moderately positive across native geometries (WXS 0.303 with negative fraction 0.019, WSI 0.134, CT 0.041, RNA 0.070), with the nearest competing set being the reciprocal candidate in every view. The pair boundary to the neighboring set is weak, but that neighbor's own membership is broadly unsupported and it is being dropped, so no remaining decision-relevant neighboring alternative materially challenges this boundary. Technical associations (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, q 0.036) are moderate and unadjusted, but they do not outweigh the coherent cross-modal membership and interpretable biology for this set. No supported split or merge remains available (allowed structural action is split only, and the internal-subdivision screen shows a dominant single-cluster resolution for this set).
